statements.text: In a recent client conversation, we talked about a landing page our team had built for their ads.
Ours was a new option, and we hadn't moved all their ad traffic over to it.
statements.source: We didn't switch all the ad traffic.

statements.text: We wanted a clear picture of how our page would convert first.
statements.source: We wanted to understand how our version would convert before making that change.

statements.text: So we compared it with the client's existing pages instead of treating them as something to retire.
statements.why: Comparison rather than switching is supported.

statements.text: We walked through changes we intended to make to it.
The revised version would go back to the client for another look before moving forward.
statements.why: Planned return for review; 'before moving forward' matches the approved claim.

statements.text: We hold the pages we build to the same scrutiny we give the pages already there.
Once we'd made those updates, I'd send it back so the client could review it again.
During a recent conversation with a client, I explained why we hadn't redirected all their ad traffic to a landing page our team had created for them.
They already had pages in their advertising, and we'd been comparing ours with those.
It's the standard we hold ourselves to in ELEVATE, our full-service advertising management program.
statements.why: Ties the client story to ELEVATE and presents it as a practice within the program; the client is not confirmed as an ELEVATE member and no source states this practice.

statements.text: When we're managing your ads, a page we created gets the same scrutiny as the pages you already have.
statements.why: States the approved stance on WIA's own work.

statements.text: We built a landing page for a client, and we didn't move all their ad traffic to it.
So on our call, I explained why we were comparing our page with their existing pages instead of switching everything over.
And I also told the client we were going to make updates to our page and send it back so they could take another look.
A landing page our team builds goes into the same evaluation as the pages you already have.
We had this exact conversation with a client recently.
statements.why: Real conversation within weeks of call.

statements.text: Whitney also described updates we intended to make to our version, and a plan to bring it back to the client for another review.
